notes: Identity: supplied canonical text identifies The zero-sum fallacy in evidence evaluation, Toby D. Pilditch, Norman Fenton and David Lagnado, with institutional affiliations, full experiments, discussion and references; source header names the UCL discovery Manuscript.pdf. This is a primary manuscript matching the neutral reference title/authors, rather than a secondary article, abstract or preregistration. DOI and journal/version/year are not printed in this supplied manuscript, so exact published-version identity cannot be independently confirmed. No PDF was supplied. Target assignment uses study_o=2 and the described negative-test/accuracy contrast, not row position or numeric matching. Locator p.6 is inconsistent with this manuscript: printed p.6 begins Experiment 1 methods; Experiment 2 target results are on printed p.11. The Experiment 2 test-result main effect reports BFInclusion4 = 607.57 (4 is a footnote marker), not d or a frequentist p. The BF is preserved as a test/evidence statistic only, not relabelled an effect size or p-value. Experiment 2 printed p.12 d-like delta values concern the exhaustiveness manipulation within each test-result group (-0.64 and -0.192), and Table 1 delta values concern comparisons with chance; none measures the target negative-versus-positive contrast. Experiment 1 printed p.8 reports delta = 1.563 for a similar negative-versus-positive comparison, but that is a different study and was not assigned to Experiment 2. Assigned es and p remain null because the target test has no printed effect-size estimate or p. Analytic N and all replication/success fields are unassigned placeholders; no sample arithmetic performed.
